title: Tensor constraints for a normalized reindexing family
statement:
theorem podReindexingTensorFamilyTensorConstraints
    (completion : ∀ {V W : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ W) [IsIso f]
      [∀ v : V, Invertible (l : V.residueField v)]
      [∀ w : W, Invertible (l : W.residueField w)], PodCompletionReindex l E f)
    (tensor : ∀ {V W : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ W) [IsIso f]
      [∀ v : V, Invertible (l : V.residueField v)]
      [∀ w : W, Invertible (l : W.residueField w)],
      PodCompletedTensorReindex l E f (completion f))
    (hcompletion : ∀ {V W : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ W) [IsIso f]
      [∀ v : V, Invertible (l : V.residueField v)]
      [∀ w : W, Invertible (l : W.residueField w)],
      PodCompletionReindex.Laws l E f (completion f))
    (htensor : ∀ {V W : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ W) [IsIso f]
      [∀ v : V, Invertible (l : V.residueField v)]
      [∀ w : W, Invertible (l : W.residueField w)],
      PodCompletedTensorReindex.Laws l E f (completion f) (tensor f))
    (identity : ∀ W : Scheme.{u}, isoReductionIntegralInverse l E (𝟙 W) ≅ 𝟭 _)
    (composition : ∀ {V W Z : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ W) (f : W ⟶ V)
      [IsIso h] [IsIso f], isoReductionIntegralInverse l E (h ≫ f) ≅
        isoReductionIntegralInverse l E f ⋙ isoReductionIntegralInverse l E h) :
    let A : PodReindexFamily l E := ⟨completion, tensor, identity, composition⟩
    ∀ {V W : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ W) [IsIso f]
      [∀ v : V, Invertible (l : V.residueField v)]
      [∀ w : W, Invertible (l : W.residueField w)], A.TensorConstraints l E f

proof.text: On each complete constructible object, the specified ordinary-to-completed map is an isomorphism: the complete-unit clause of hcompletion inverts the adjunction unit, ordinary reindexing preserves that isomorphism, and the two remaining factors are components of the given limit and pullback isomorphisms. Use the intrinsic/legacy completeness equivalence to supply the complete-input predicate. Restrict these components and their naturality to the constructible full subcategories.

The Canonical clause of htensor says precisely that this natural isomorphism intertwines the given tensor comparison with the canonical integral completed pullback comparison. Package the latter as a natural isomorphism using its proved naturality.

Transport the canonical associativity and braiding equations across the natural isomorphism. Tensor bifunctoriality and naturality of the target associator and braiding identify the transported paths. The existing general reduced_associativity and reduced_braiding calculations apply with identity reduction functors. Associator naturality follows from the existing faithful-reduction calculation and the normalized reduction equation.

Take the canonical integral pullback unit isomorphism and precompose it with the ordinary-to-completed component at the source unit. For either unitor, postcompose the required equation with the invertible ordinary-to-completed component of its input. Naturality of the target unitor, tensor bifunctoriality, the Canonical clause and the canonical unitor equation give equality. Cancel the component. Left-unitor naturality is reflected by faithful coherent reduction; use the existing proved integral right-unitor naturality calculation for the right side. These arguments require no nonzero object or inhabited scheme.

proof_origin.place: Steps 1 and 5; shorter route transporting the already normalized canonical integral tensor coherence along the specified ordinary-to-completed natural isomorphism.
